title: Actuation Safety Declaration V1.0
description: What the Implementer of an Actuation Unit declares for its vehicle: the safe state it takes the vehicle to, when it does so, and the limits it keeps. The Unit shall have a declaration, and none of the required properties may be omitted: the safety rules of the Unit are fixed by its Specification, the values are the Implementer's.

UnitID.description: Identifier of the Unit, and of the vehicle it acts on.

SafeState.description: The state the Unit takes the vehicle to, without the Module, from any state.

Kind.description: The vehicle is brought to a standstill within its limits and held. A vehicle in motion is never left as it was last told. Any other manoeuvre, such as pulling over, is the Module's.

StopDeceleration.description: Deceleration (m/s2) with which the vehicle is brought to a standstill in the safe state.

HoldMethod.description: How the vehicle is held once it stands: parking brake, brake pressure, and the like.

TimeToSafeState.description: The longest time (s) from the cause to the vehicle standing, from the speed at which the vehicle is allowed to move. It is bounded and declared.

CommandTimeout.description: Milliseconds without a valid command, after which the Unit takes the vehicle to its safe state. It is shorter than the margin the vehicle has to stop.

MaxCommandAge.description: Milliseconds. A command older than this, by its time stamp, is not executed: it is discarded and counted.

ResponsePeriod.description: Milliseconds between the Responses the Unit gives. A Response that is not given within it is a fault of the Unit.

Limits.description: What the vehicle can be asked to do. A command beyond a limit is limited to it, and recorded.

ReArm.description: How the Unit takes commands again after it has been in its safe state.

Authority.description: Only the User Agent re-arms the Unit, on an act of a person. The Module cannot, and the Unit does not re-arm itself.

Procedure.description: What the act is, and what the Unit checks before it takes a command.

Override.description: The sources of a human override of the vehicle - a pedal, a wheel, a button -, which always prevail over the commands, and which the Unit reports.
